Why I am building this
Chapter 1 · Ladakh

It started on the road to Ladakh.

The ride of a lifetime. I spent more time planning it than riding it.

1

Planning lived in ten places

Routes in maps, fuel stops in a sheet, permits in my gallery, advice in old forums.

2

Fuel was a guess

Long gaps between pumps, and no record of what the bike really used at altitude.

3

Off the grid, off the radar

Hours without signal. Nobody at home, or in our group, could see us.

02 / 15

The founder's own ride. These pains are being tested in structured rider interviews.

Why I am building this
Chapter 2 · Bengaluru

Then every weekend became a search.

Bengaluru is ringed by ghats, coffee estates and dirt trails. Finding them, and trusting them, is the hard part.

1

Trails hide in reels

The best routes live in posts, DMs and word of mouth, never in one trusted place.

2

Can I ride it this weekend?

Is it open, legal, rideable after rain? A pin on a map cannot tell you.

3

Saturdays lost to scrolling

Hours of planning for a three-hour ride, then the same old highway.

03 / 15

Why I am building this
Chapter 3 · The group ride

And every group ride lost someone.

Riding together is the best part of the sport, and the most chaotic.

1

"Where are you?"

Calls at 80 km/h, and a shared location frozen twenty minutes ago.

2

Nobody sees the whole group

The lead cannot see who dropped back. The sweep cannot see where the lead turned.

3

When something goes wrong

A fall in a dead zone, and the group finds out at the next chai stop.

04 / 15

Myto Moto is the app I wanted on each of those rides.

Market

India buys a million big bikes a year. Nobody built their software.

Premium motorcycles are India's fastest-growing two-wheeler segment, and their riders spend on the ride.

Bought every year

Motorcycles above 250 cc sold in India in FY25. Royal Enfield alone sold 9 lakh at home.

Sold11 lakh

Riders on the road

Five years of big-bike sales: riders who tour, ride in groups and buy gear.

Base50 lakh+

Our beachhead

Weekend riders and clubs around our verified trails. Then Pune, Delhi NCR and Mumbai.

StartBengaluru
08 / 15

11 lakh ≈ Royal Enfield's 9.03 lakh FY25 domestic sales at its 80%+ share of 250 cc+. 50 lakh+ is our five-year estimate. Sources: Eicher Motors FY25; Autocar Pro; CareEdge FY25 report.

Why now

Riders are upgrading. Their tools are not.

Four shifts make this the moment for a rider-first platform.

  • Premium is booming

    Bikes above 150 cc grew from 14% to 19% of motorcycle sales, FY19 to FY25.

  • Touring went mainstream

    Ladakh drew 6.1 lakh domestic tourists in 2024. Riding there is a rite of passage.

  • Clubs run on chat

    Group rides, payments and safety are coordinated in chats never built for it.

  • The phone is enough

    Offline maps, background GPS and SOS now work with no extra hardware.

Premium share: Crisil, via Autocar Pro. Ladakh arrivals: Government data tabled in the Lok Sabha.

Business modelHypothesis

A free core builds the network. Revenue comes from those who get the most value.

VisionPlanned

From app to rider brand.

The app earns the rider's trust. The brand earns a place in the garage.

  • Next
